newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Japan, Indonesia pledge mutual cooperation.
newsitem.headline: Japan, Indonesia pledge mutual cooperation.

text.p: The leaders of Japan and Indonesia pledged mutual cooperation on Thursday, with both stressing the importance of ties between Tokyo and Southeast Asian countries.

Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto told an official dinner hosted by Indonesia's President Suharto that the expected expansion of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) "provides the core for dramatic regional cooperation".

"It is precisely in such a time of transformation that it becomes all the more essential for our two countries to further strengthen our ties and join hands working for stability and prosperity in the Asia-Pacific region," Hashimoto said in his prepared address.

Hashimoto is being accompanied by a task force with communications equipment to keep him in constant contact with Tokyo and Peru, where Marxist rebels are holding hostages in the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima.

Suharto thanked Japan -- Indonesia's biggest trading partner and aid donor -- for its "whole-hearted help" in his country's development, and said cooperation between ASEAN and Japan had given a boost to economic growth in the region.

"We should maintain such cooperation, we should improve and develop it in terms of shape and content in order to face challenges and benefit from opportunities emerging from recent rapid changes," the veteran Indonesian leader said.
Hashimoto earlier arrived in Jakarta from Malaysia on the third leg of a five-nation Southeast Asian tour. He has also visited Brunei and will go on to Vietnam on Saturday before visiting Singapore.
On his current trip, Hashimoto is visiting ASEAN members Brunei, Malaysia, Indonesia, Vietnam and Singapore. He visited the group's other two members, Thailand and the Philippines, last year.
The prime minister and Suharto will get down to substantive discussions on Friday covering bilateral, regional and global issues, diplomats said.
In initial talks on Thursday, Suharto and Hashimoto agreed that terrorism must be opposed or the pattern of violence would continue.

Indonesia's State Secretary Murdiono told reporters: "Both leaders agreed we must not give in to terrorism, because if the demands of terrorists were met, this would become a pattern and lead to similar demands in the future."
In his dinner speech, Suharto said Japan had actively contributed to peace, stability and prosperity in Asia and the Pacific.
Japan's participation in the ASEAN Regional Forum (ARF) defence consultative grouping had been "very positive and gives benefit to all parties", Southeast Asia's elder statesman said.
"We gladly welcome your policy of giving priority to your closest Asian neighbours," he told Hashimoto.
